:::{#thm-kolmogorov-uncomputable}
#### Kolmogorov complexity cannot be computed

No program takes a binary string $x$ as input and outputs $K(x)$.

:::

::: {.proof}
Suppose a program $Q$ outputs $K(x)$ on input $x$.
For each integer $m \ge 1$, consider the program $P_m$ that does the following:
list binary strings in order of length,
use $Q$ to compute $K(x)$ for each one,
and output the first $x$ with $K(x) \ge m$.
Such an $x$ exists, because fewer than $2^m$ programs are shorter than $m$,
so $P_m$ halts, and its output $x$ has $K(x) \ge m$.

The program $P_m$ consists of a fixed part, of some length $c$,
and a description of $m$ that shows where it ends,
which the proof of @thm-kolmogorov-upper-bound writes in at most $2 \log_2 m + 4$ digits.
So the output $x$ of $P_m$ also has $K(x) \le 2 \log_2 m + 4 + c$, and together

$$m \le K(x) \le 2 \log_2 m + 4 + c.$$

The left side grows faster than the right,
so this fails once $m$ is large enough,
and no such $Q$ exists.
The argument formalizes the Berry paradox,
"the smallest positive integer not definable in under sixty letters",
and @cover2006elements [chapter 14] discuss why $K$ cannot be computed.

:::
